glance: 125 km to Sirajganj by road, 3–5 hours by bus or car
elliott-bridge-sirajganj.desc: Elliott Bridge, which locals call Boropool, spans the Katakhali (Boral) river that splits Sirajganj town in two. Its foundation stone was laid in 1892 by Charles Alfred Elliott, Lieutenant Governor of Bengal, after whom it is named. The bridge is a single steel arch about 160 feet long and 30 feet high, built without pillars so that large cargo boats could pass beneath. Heavy vehicles are no longer allowed on it, and since the river was re-excavated in 2019 water flows under it again.
blocks: How to get there
It is in the middle of Sirajganj town; any rickshaw will take you to Boropool.
Good to know
Come in the evening when the town is lively. Watch out for traffic on the narrow deck.

potajia-navaratna-temple.desc: This temple stands in Potajia village, about 5 km west of Shahzadpur. Gobindaram Roy, a diwan from the wealthy local Roy family, built it as the family's place of worship around 1700. It rises about 30 feet in three storeys and is called navaratna because it once had nine chambers. The walls carried terracotta panels and images of gods. After the family left for India in 1947 the temple fell into decay, and the Department of Archaeology took it over in 1954.
blocks: How to get there
From Shahzadpur take an auto-rickshaw about 5 km west to Potajia village.
Good to know
Potajia is also dairy country, so the drive passes green pastures. Do not climb on the structure.

glance: 125 km to Sirajganj by road, 3–5 hours by bus or car
sirajganj-handloom.desc: Sirajganj is one of the biggest handloom areas in Bangladesh, centred on Belkuchi, Enayetpur, Chauhali and Shahzadpur. In many homes the clack of wooden looms starts early and runs into the night, producing lungis, cotton sarees and gamchhas. Colourful yarn hangs out to dry along the lanes, and weekly cloth markets draw wholesalers from far away. Visitors can watch weavers at work and buy directly at fair prices.
blocks: How to get there
From Sirajganj town take a CNG or bus south to Belkuchi or Enayetpur.
Good to know
Ask before photographing inside homes. Weavers are busiest before Eid.

glance: The drying yards around Mohishluti fish depot (arot), Tarash upazila, Sirajganj, from October to December
mohishluti-chalan-beel-shutki.desc: When the Chalan Beel water drops at the start of winter, small fish such as puti, taki and shol are cleaned, salted lightly and laid out on bamboo racks to dry around the Mohishluti fish depot in Tarash upazila. Unlike sea shutki, this freshwater kind is milder and is cooked as a bhuna or a mashed bhorta with chilli and garlic. A good share goes to India, but the depot and nearby drying yards sell to anyone. Catches vary a lot from year to year, so stock and prices change with the season.
blocks: Good to know
Puti shutki is the cheapest and most common; shol and boal cost much more.

glance: 125 km to Sirajganj by road, 3–5 hours by bus or car
jamuna-bridge.desc: Opened in 1998 and long known as the Bangabandhu Bridge, this road and rail bridge is one of the longest in South Asia. It spans the Jamuna between Bhuapur in Tangail and Sirajganj, ending a long dependence on ferries. A separate dedicated rail bridge has since been built alongside it. From the western approach and nearby riverbanks you can watch the wide, shifting river and its sandy chars.
blocks: How to get there
Buses between Dhaka and the north cross it; the western approach is near Saidabad in Sirajganj Sadar.
Good to know
Stopping on the bridge is not allowed. Enjoy the view from the riverbank parks near the western end.

glance: 125 km to Sirajganj by road, 3–5 hours by bus or car
jamuna-bridge-west-eco-park.desc: The eco park lies at Saidabad in Sirajganj Sadar, next to the embankment on the west bank of the Jamuna and north of the highway. After the bridge was built, the Forest Department planted trees around its approaches, and in 2007 about 124 acres were set aside as an eco park, opened in March 2008. Today it is a green, shady place where families picnic and walk, with the long bridge and the wide river close by.
blocks: How to get there
Take a bus or CNG from Sirajganj town to Saidabad near the western end of the bridge.
Good to know
Weekday mornings are quiet. Stay off the bridge approach road itself.

shahzadpur-kachharibari.desc: Shahzadpur was one of the Tagore family's estates, and Rabindranath spent periods here in the 1890s managing it. He wrote several poems, stories and letters during these stays, drawing on the river life around him. The two-storey building with its wide verandahs is now a museum with furniture, photographs and personal items. Each year Tagore's birthday is celebrated here with music and a fair.
blocks: How to get there
Shahzadpur is on the Dhaka–Bogura side of the river; take a bus to Shahzadpur and a rickshaw to the Kachharibari.
Good to know
Check the weekly closing day. Combine with a visit to the weaving villages nearby.

shahzadpur-dargah-mosque.desc: This old mosque stands on the west bank of the Hurasagar river in Shahzadpur, about 2 km east of the Bogura–Nagarbari road. It is a single hall, wide from north to south, with five doorways on the east side. Inside, eight stone pillars divide the room into fifteen bays, each covered by its own dome. Next to it are the shrines of Hazrat Makhdum Shah Dowla and Shamsuddin Tabrizi, and pilgrims come throughout the year.
blocks: How to get there
Take a bus to Shahzadpur, then a rickshaw to the Dargah area by the Hurasagar.
Good to know
Visit together with the Rabindra Kachharibari in Shahzadpur. Dress modestly and avoid prayer times.

glance: Dairy and sweet shops in Shahzadpur and Ullapara
winter (Dec–Jan), spring (Feb–Mar), summer (Apr–May), monsoon (Jun–Jul), autumn (Aug–Sep) and late autumn (Oct–Nov)
sirajganj-dairy-ghee.desc: The low pastures around Shahzadpur, Ullapara and the edge of Chalan Beel are one of Bangladesh's main dairy areas, with thousands of small farms. The national milk cooperative has a large plant at Baghabari, collecting milk from across the area. Locally, the milk becomes ghee, sweet doi, sweets and fresh butter. Morning milk markets, with cans arriving by bicycle and boat, are a lively sight.
blocks: Good to know
Buy ghee from established shops to avoid adulteration.

glance: Sweet shops in Enayetpur and Sirajganj town
winter (Dec–Jan), spring (Feb–Mar), summer (Apr–May), monsoon (Jun–Jul), autumn (Aug–Sep) and late autumn (Oct–Nov)
enayetpur-pantua.desc: Pantua is made from chhana and a little flour, shaped into balls, fried until deep brown and then soaked in sugar syrup. Sirajganj's version is soft inside with a slightly firm skin. Local tradition credits a sweet maker of Enayetpur with creating it about a century ago, and his family's shop still operates there. Sweet shops in Sirajganj town also make their own.
blocks: Good to know
Ask for it warm, fresh from the syrup.

hatikumrul-navaratna-temple.desc: The Navaratna, or nine-jewelled, temple is a three-storey brick tower crowned with nine small spires, built in the 18th century. Traces of terracotta work survive on its walls. Most travellers rush past Hatikumrul, one of the country's busiest road junctions, without knowing it is there. It stands among fields and smaller temples, a calm contrast to the highway traffic.
blocks: How to get there
From Hatikumrul junction in Ullapara upazila, take a rickshaw or auto-rickshaw a couple of kilometres along the village road.
Good to know
Good stop to break a long road journey to the north.

glance: 125 km to Sirajganj by road, 3–5 hours by bus or car
sirajganj-hard-point.desc: Sirajganj town has long fought erosion from the Jamuna, and the protective embankment known as Hard Point is now its favourite promenade. Concrete blocks slope down to the water, and the view opens across a seemingly endless river. In the evening people come for tea, snacks and the breeze, and boats can be hired for short trips. During the monsoon the current is powerful and the river feels like a sea.
blocks: How to get there
On the eastern edge of Sirajganj town; any rickshaw will take you.
Good to know
Stay off the slippery blocks in the rain. Avoid boat trips in rough weather.
